lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Reception. The lobby smells like new carpet over an old building. A wall of awards, none dated later than eighteen months ago.

lines.speaker: joan
lines.text: Morning. You'll be the new project manager? Marcus is expecting you — go on up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She says it plainly, the way she'd say it to anyone. She doesn't know you yet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Upstairs, the office is quieter than a company mid-crisis has any right to be. A desk near the window still has a mug on it — half-full, gone cold. Nobody's moved it. Nobody's sitting there either.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: You made it. Good — we need every pair of hands we can get right now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She's already gone before you can answer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Marcus is waiting, door open. He doesn't get up.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: You must be the new PM. Ellis's replacement.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A beat. He says the name like it costs him something small every time.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Sit down. Before you ask me anything—

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: —tell me what you think is wrong with this project.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He watches you. Not impatient. Testing.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Because something clearly is. You just haven't found it yet.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: That's not important right now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He looks back down at the folder on his desk, like the conversation's already over.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: What's important is whether you can tell me what's wrong with this project. Start looking.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Good. Start wherever you like. Emails, Teams, the shared drive — it's all a mess, take your pick.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He hesitates, like there's a second sentence he's deciding whether to say.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: The Board wants an update in six days. I'd rather you found the problem before they did.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He turns back to his screen. The conversation, such as it was, is over — but you notice he still hasn't touched the mug.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Fine. That's the external picture. What about us?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He nods at the corkboard behind him — half-empty, waiting.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats. Yours to fill in. Don't flatter us.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You lay it out plainly: a Board that trusts speed over process, a Quality lead nobody's briefed properly yet, and a delivery team that hasn't worked together before this week.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...You're not wrong.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You go looking for the original Business Case to check it against what you've found. The main document opens fine. The appendices don't exist.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You search Ellis's old email account. Then Teams. Then the shared drive again — further in this time, past the folder you already found.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Buried three folders deep: a partially finished document. "Benefits_Plan_DRAFT_v3." Last edited nine days before Ellis resigned. It stops mid-sentence.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tucked behind it, a single scanned page — handwriting, not typed. A notebook page, out of place among the spreadsheets.

lines.speaker: ellis
lines.text: “They want a plan. What they need is someone who'll tell them the truth before it's too late.”

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You don't know yet what that means. You have a feeling you're going to.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: So. What's your diagnosis?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Monday. The coffee machine is doing that thing again — the one where it decides sugar is optional whether you asked for it or not.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: You look like you survived the Board.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A small laugh, more relief than humour.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Barely, right? Marcus was in a mood all morning. Something about scope.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She takes her coffee, pauses.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: You'll figure out fast that nobody here agrees on what this project actually needs. Buckle up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She's gone before you can ask what she means.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By the time you reach the boardroom, you understand. This was never just a construction project. Somewhere between the concrete and the contract, it became a negotiation.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Right. Let's get this done. Everyone's had the requirements list — today we decide what actually gets built.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Every automation line on that list is a Must. I'm not being dramatic — the throughput targets don't work without them.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Every one of those "Musts" has a number next to it, Priya. I've added them up. You're proposing we double the budget before we've poured a foundation.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: And validation isn't on that list at all yet. I'd like to fix that before we talk about anything else.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: One thing at a time. You're chairing this — talk us through it.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: You've just doubled the budget.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: So automation's a "Should" now? That's going to hit us in commissioning, not now — when it's expensive to fix.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Automation as a Must. Thank you — that's going to save us weeks in commissioning.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Camille cuts in before Marcus can respond.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: Actually — I'd rather we under-build automation than under-build validation. We can automate a working line later. We can't un-fail an inspection.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The room goes quiet. Marcus looks between them — this isn't a fight he called.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...Noted, Camille. Final call. Does the board stand as it is, or are you changing it?

DIALOGUE_ACT2_SCENE02_POST.engineNote: Line 1 (moscow_overcommitted) only fires if 6+ of 8 MoSCoW cards ended up in Must (EV-E3). Lines 2/3 are mutually exclusive on automation_marked_must (set by the MoSCoW tool screen, first card). Exactly one of 2/3 should render before Camille's interruption.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: That went about as well as I expected. Camille doesn't interrupt me for nothing, by the way. Remember that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He says it like a warning. Or an observation. Hard to tell which.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Before we go further — I want you to think about something most PMs get wrong. Who's actually going to stop this project if they disagree with it? Not who signs it off. Who can actually kill it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He waits, arms crossed.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Map it. Power, interest, all of it. Then tell me if you're surprised by what you find.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player builds the stakeholder power/interest grid.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You expect Marcus's name at the top. It isn't, not quite. Daniel's budget authority reaches further than anyone admitted out loud in that room. And Camille — Camille doesn't need permission to escalate anything. She's never used it. Yet.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Now you're starting to see it.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: Right, quick one before I get back out there. Electrical contractor's gone quiet. Two weeks, no update, calls not returned.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He says it like it's nothing. It isn't nothing.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: While we're raising things — the validation timeline in the current plan assumes everything goes right first time. Nothing ever goes right first time.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: And the contingency line is thinner than I'd like for a project this size. I said so at the business case stage. I'm saying it again now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three problems, three people who'd rather not be the one holding all of them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player builds the Risk Register from the three risks just raised.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You tag the contractor as a risk, not just a rumour. Vaughn looks faintly relieved someone wrote it down.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: ...Appreciate that, actually.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: One more decision before we start moving dirt. Are we running this like a traditional construction project — staged, sign-off at every gate? Or something with more give in it?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He's not being rhetorical. He actually wants to know what you think.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Pick wrong and it'll cost us later. Pick right and nobody will ever notice you made a decision at all. That's usually how it goes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Late, after everyone's gone, you're still in the site office finishing paperwork when you find it — a folder inside a folder, easy to miss unless you're looking. "Risk_Register_OLD.xlsx." Half-finished. Ellis's initials in the file metadata.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One line jumps out, highlighted in yellow, like Ellis meant to come back to it and never did.

lines.speaker: ellis
lines.text: “Marcus doesn't want certainty. He wants confidence.”

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You think about the Board meeting. About Camille's “Actually—”. About the version of this project where somebody told Marcus what he wanted to hear instead of what was true.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You don't know yet if that's what happened to Ellis. But you're starting to have a theory.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: Right. C'mere. Better you see it than I describe it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He leads you across the concrete floor, boots echoing. Overhead, the first steel frame sections are already up — the building's actual bones, finally visible instead of theoretical.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: Walk me through everything that needs to happen before we can manufacture medicine in this room. Everything. I'm not being polite — if you miss something, we both find out the expensive way, later.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player drags work packages onto the board: Construction, Utilities, Equipment, Validation, Training, Documentation.]

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: ...Not bad. Most people forget documentation until the end. It's not the end. It's the whole time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He glances up at the frame overhead, something briefly unguarded in his face.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: My daughter starts here next month, actually. Graduate scheme. First proper job.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He doesn't say anything else about it. He doesn't need to.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Every box you just added costs money. Let's find out how much.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He pulls up the WBS on a second monitor, converting each work package into a line item without looking away from the screen.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Some of this I can defend to the Board blind. Some of it I'm going to need you to explain to me first, so I don't get blindsided explaining it to them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A pause. He finally looks up.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: I've had two rounds of headcount cuts on my own team this year. I'd rather the third round wasn't caused by a project I signed off badly.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He says it flatly, like a fact rather than a complaint, and goes back to the spreadsheet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player builds the Cost Breakdown Structure from the WBS.]

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: ...Alright. This I can work with.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Budget for six people. Pick wisely — you won't get a seventh if this goes sideways.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He slides a folder of candidate profiles across the desk.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Some of them are better than their CVs. Some of them are worse. You'll have to guess right more than once.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player selects 6 of a wider candidate pool.]

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Good enough. Try not to lose any of them.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: Whiteboard's yours. Whatever you put up here, we're building to it — so don't put anything up you don't believe.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player arranges milestones on a timeline.]

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: ...That's tight, but I've built to tighter. Just don't tell Marcus I said that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Later, filing your own timeline notes next to Vaughn's old ones, you find a scrap you missed before — half a page, tucked where a completed page should be.

lines.speaker: ellis
lines.text: “If Vaughn says a name's gone quiet, that name is already gone.”

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You think of the contractor you logged as a risk two weeks ago, not just a rumour. You hope that was enough.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: How often do you want to update me?

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: I don't want another dashboard. I want decisions.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Priya, half-listening from across the room, chimes in without looking up from her tablet.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Ops wants weekly meetings. Actual meetings, not an email nobody reads.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: Site wants daily stand-ups. Five minutes, not thirty.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everyone wants something slightly different, and all of it, apparently, from you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player builds the Communications Plan, matching cadence and format to each stakeholder.]

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Fine. Let's see if you can actually keep to it.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: How are we actually proving this project was worth twelve million pounds?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Not hostile. Genuinely asking.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Because "we built a building" isn't a benefit. Patients treated is a benefit. Contract secured is a benefit. I need you to point at those and say why, specifically, this got us there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player builds the Benefits Register, linking outputs to outcomes.]

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: ...This is the first version of this document that's actually made me feel better about our chances.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three companies want the isolator contract. Tomasz has arranged back-to-back pitches, the way you'd schedule dentist appointments you're dreading.

lines.speaker: tomasz
lines.text: SteriTech first. Fair warning — they don't do sales pitches, they do specs. Try to keep up.

lines.speaker: steritech_rep
lines.text: We're not the exciting option. We're the option that's still standing when the exciting ones aren't. Cheapest bid, proven kit, nothing fancy.

lines.speaker: rapidform_rep
lines.text: Installed and validated four weeks faster than anyone else in this room can promise you. Time is the one thing you can't buy back later.

lines.speaker: pharmacraft_rep
lines.text: Every unit we've shipped in the last five years passed first-time validation. Every one. We'd like to keep that record intact with you.

lines.speaker: tomasz
lines.text: There isn't a wrong answer here, technically. There's just the one you'll be living with.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Across the office, someone's clapping. Camille, mostly out of view, has just been told she's won an industry award for a paper on validation risk she wrote two years ago and forgot she'd submitted.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: ...Oh. Well. That's unexpected.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's a strange, small moment of good news in the middle of a decision that has none of the easy kind.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three weeks into construction proper, and for exactly nine days, everything holds. Then it doesn't.

lines.speaker: tomasz
lines.text: The isolator's delayed. Confirmed this morning.

lines.speaker: tomasz
lines.text: There's no version of this where you keep both the timeline and the budget. I've already asked.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Remember the filling line we put through the Board back in week two? I'd like the actual go-ahead now — the room's ready.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: We already agreed to that one, didn't we?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Small ask. We squeeze one more filling line into the room — same footprint, better throughput. I've already checked it fits.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I like it. If it fits, we should—

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: Actually — no. Not without a full revalidation of the cleanroom classification. That's not a formality. That's weeks.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: I'd want a full revalidation of the cleanroom classification before we agree to that. That's not a formality. That's weeks.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Camille—

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: I'm not saying no. I'm saying not for free.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The room waits on you.

DIALOGUE_ACT4_SCENE03.sourceSummary: Week 18. Everything is going well. Marcus walks in: the Board has bought a second pharmaceutical company and wants NOVA to manufacture two products instead of one. Scope, benefits, risk, timeline and politics all move at once.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The weeks that follow don't have a shape you'd recognise as a plan anymore. They have a shape more like weather.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Somewhere in the middle of it, you stop being surprised by the pace and start being surprised by what you're still standing after.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The first report is easy. Nothing's gone wrong enough yet to be a real test.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: How's my project?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The last events before commissioning don't ask your permission. They just happen, and you find out which parts of the plan were actually load-bearing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One evening, Camille catches you still in the office and, unprompted, hands you a photocopy — not from her own notes, but from Ellis's. She's had it a while, she says. She wasn't sure when to give it to you.

lines.speaker: ellis
lines.text: “Camille will never be the problem. She'll be the only one still standing when there is one.”

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: He was right about that, for what it's worth.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Somewhere in the last few weeks, this stopped being Ellis's mess you inherited. It's just yours now.

DIALOGUE_ACT4_SCENE06.engineNote: Hands off to late-wave Act 4 events (EV-07, EV-09, EV-10, EV-14, EV-15) per their own conditions — dialogue/choices for those individual events still need writing. Ellis Fragment #5 is conditional on camilleTrust_high and may not be found this playthrough, by design.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: Come see this properly. Not through a hard hat and a headache.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The building doesn't look like a building anymore. It looks like what it was meant to be.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: Both lines are physically ready. Whether they're actually ready is your department now, not mine.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player runs the commissioning and training checklist across both product lines.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gaps you left earlier — a validation step deferred, a training session compressed to save a day — don't announce themselves. They just don't check out clean.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You go looking for the paper trail — not because you doubt it exists, but because you're about to be asked to produce it, and “I'm sure it's somewhere” has never satisfied an inspector.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: This is the part nobody enjoys and everybody needs. Validation records, change logs, risk responses — all of it, in order, ready to be read by someone who wasn't in the room when any of it happened.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Player assembles the audit trail.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Some of what you find is exactly as thorough as you remember making it. Some of it isn't. You didn't always know, at the time, which decisions would matter later.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: Whitfield's team arrives Thursday. Whatever's not here by then isn't here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inspector Whitfield doesn't waste time on pleasantries. Four questions. That's usually how it goes.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Walk me through the extra filling line. Who approved it, and what was assessed before that happened?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You produce the Change Control record — cost, schedule, quality impact, all assessed before Marcus signed off.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Thorough. Good.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There's no approved change to show, because you didn't approve one.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Then there's nothing to review here. Also acceptable.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Second. Show me your stakeholder analysis.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You hand over the power/interest map you built in your second week — the one where you first noticed Daniel and Camille had more real leverage than the room let on.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: ...You mapped Daniel's budget authority correctly. Most people miss that one.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Third. The isolator delay, early in delivery — how was that resolved, and what did it cost?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You show the expedite approval, dated, costed, signed off the same day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You show the revised schedule, and the message where you told Marcus it would slip, in writing, before it slipped.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Either's defensible. What isn't defensible is doing one and reporting the other. You didn't. Noted.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: Last one. Do any of your own status reports say something the rest of the record doesn't support?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Whitfield finds it before you can explain it away — the month you said “on track” while your own risk log said otherwise.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: This one concerns me more than the others.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You don't have a good answer. There isn't one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Whitfield checks. Checks again. Doesn't find anything.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: No, they don't. That's rarer than you'd think.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: For what it's worth — people here describe you fairly consistently. That's not nothing, in an audit.

lines.speaker: whitfield
lines.text: That's everything I need for today.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She doesn't say anything else. Inspectors generally don't.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inspector Whitfield's team leaves without a word about outcome. That's normal. It still feels like something.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The office doesn't quite know what to do with itself. Nobody starts a new task. Nobody quite finishes an old one either.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Marcus stands by the window, not really looking at anything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Priya reorganises the same folder three times.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Camille reads the same page for what must be the fourth time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody says the word “inspection” out loud for the rest of the day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The phone rings.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Marcus answers it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He doesn't speak. He listens. For a long time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then he slowly smiles.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Fade to black.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: THREE WEEKS LATER.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The building looks finished now, in the way buildings only look finished once people are actually using them instead of building them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [Facility Progress final reel plays: Week 1's empty warehouse through to Week 24's medicine on the line, side by side.]

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inspector Whitfield was never testing your memory. She was testing your paperwork — because paperwork is just decisions, written down so someone else can trust them later.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You're about to find out if yours held up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everyone who can fit is in the control room. Marcus. Camille. Vaughn — and, if you did right by him, his daughter, hovering near the back, trying not to look as nervous as she clearly is. Priya. Daniel. Tomasz. Aisha.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Vaughn keeps glancing toward the door.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The line starts.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Silence. Nobody talks over the hum of equipment actually running, for the first time, doing the thing it was built to do.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Screens show the batch progressing. Green, then green, then green.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Quality Control waits with the rest of you. Waiting is apparently the same for everyone, regardless of job title.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Finally — results.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: BATCH RELEASED.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Someone — you're not sure who first — starts clapping. Then everyone does.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...Right. Go on, all of you. You've earned five minutes of this before I put you back to work.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: BATCH REJECTED.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The clapping that was already starting dies half-formed.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: It's a quality flag, not a catastrophe. We find out why, and we fix it.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...Right.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: NHS contract's confirmed. Board's thrilled. For what it's worth — I wasn't sure anyone could actually pull this off. Including you, some weeks.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Ellis couldn't, in the end. You could. I don't say that to make you feel good. I say it because it's true — and I don't like surprises, remember.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Contract's secured. Margin's thinner than what we promised the Board, but it's real.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He doesn't smile exactly. More like the absence of worry, which on Daniel passes for the same thing. The team looks like people who won something that cost more than they expected.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: We lost it. Competitor got there first.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: You told me the truth the whole way through, even when it cost you. That's worth more to me than the contract, and I mean that — though I'd rather have had both.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There will be another project. This one's just over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The first batch fails on a technicality. Camille has the root cause identified within the day — your documentation made it fast.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: Second batch, three weeks. This is fixable. It's fixed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The batch fails, and the evidence trail is too thin to explain why quickly. The Board pauses the programme pending external review.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I have to reassign you. This isn't personal.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It doesn't feel like it's not personal. You think, not for the first time, of Ellis's desk. The mug that never got moved.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The building works. The politics didn't. A rival executive, whose name you can now put to several small moments of friction over the last six months, has quietly had you moved off the project before launch.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I fought this. Same as before.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You believe him. It doesn't change anything.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The concern nobody addressed properly in Act 4 became a formal external investigation, and it overtook the project's own timeline entirely.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody in the control room is celebrating today. They're answering questions instead.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Here's what the building remembers about you:

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: — Joan's greeting, this morning, whatever it was.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: — Vaughn's site crew, waving or not waving, the last time you crossed the floor.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: — Daniel, auditing your figures or trusting them outright.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: — A Board member, somewhere, quoting a decision you made months ago back to you as though it were obvious.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: — The status report Inspector Whitfield asked about, and whether it held up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Late, packing up the last of your things from the desk you've had for months now, you find one more page. The last one.

lines.speaker: ellis
lines.text: “I thought if I just held the line long enough, it would hold itself. It didn't. Whoever reads this — you'll do better. Or you won't. Either way, nobody does this one perfectly.”

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ellis Grant wasn't removed for being a bad project manager. They were carrying the exact same pressures you just survived — sponsor expectations, regulation, budget, constant change — alone, for far longer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You didn't beat Ellis. You survived the same project.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Project management was never about finding the perfect answer. It was about making informed decisions, under real pressure, with people who didn't always agree with you — including the ones who turned out to be right, and the ones who turned out to be wrong, including yourself.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Marcus doesn't sit down.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I need five minutes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He doesn't wait for a response.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: The Board closed on an acquisition this morning. A generics manufacturer — Corvane Pharma.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He lets that sit for a second longer than feels comfortable.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: They want NOVA to manufacture Corvane's flagship product as well. Both lines. Same facility. Same timeline.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Silence.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Both? Marcus, we costed one product line. Not two.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I know what we costed, Daniel.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He turns to face the player directly.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I fought this. I lost. The Board's already told the market — this is happening. The only question left is how.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three hundred and forty-one unread. Ellis stopped answering two weeks before he left.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You open Teams. The project channel goes quiet exactly nine days before the resignation email.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You find a folder labelled "DRAFT — do not send." It's dated the day Ellis left.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Well? What have you found?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Tomorrow's Board meeting isn't routine. They want to know if anything's changed outside these walls since the business case was approved.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He slides a folder across the desk. It's thin. Thinner than a project this size should have.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Steel. Regulation. Funding. Demand. Somebody upstairs is going to ask if any of it still holds up. I'd like an answer that isn't "we didn't check."

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: So — which lens do you want to look through?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...That's more than I expected you to find in a day.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Good enough to start with.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He stands, finally, jacket already half on.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: One thing. Never surprise me. Whatever you find from here — however bad — I hear it from you first. Not from the Board. Not from a status report I'm reading in the room.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He holds the door.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Don't make me regret hiring Ellis's replacement twice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Whatever you chose, it's the first real crack in a plan that looked, three weeks ago, like it might hold together cleanly. It won't be the last.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Later that week, clearing space for a new supplier folder, you find something that isn't a supplier folder. Another page, same handwriting as before.

lines.speaker: ellis
lines.text: “Scope only ever grows. Budget for that, not for the plan you were given.”

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You fold it into the growing stack of things Ellis apparently knew and never got to act on. You wonder, not for the first time, whether knowing was ever really the problem.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A month later, less holds.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I asked for one thing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He doesn't raise his voice. He doesn't need to.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Never mind. Just tell me now.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: How's my project?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A third report follows before commissioning starts in earnest. By now, you've learned whether honesty costs you less than the alternative — or more.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: The cleanroom design failed GMP review. Not close. Failed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She lets it land before continuing.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: We can rework it now, appeal the finding, or phase the fix around commissioning and hope nobody asks before we're ready.

lines.speaker: tomasz
lines.text: Residents are complaining about the construction traffic. Local paper's asking questions.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Investors are coming. Not next quarter — Thursday.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He already looks like he's rehearsing something in his head.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: Contamination. During commissioning. I need a decision, not a discussion.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: The electrical contractor's gone under. Actually gone, this time.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: At least we saw it coming.

lines.speaker: vaughn
lines.text: Loading bay's flooded. Half the delivered equipment's sitting in six inches of water.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: New MHRA guidance dropped this morning. We need to check we still comply.

lines.speaker: tomasz
lines.text: Supplier shipped the wrong voltage spec. Whole pallet.

lines.speaker: tomasz
lines.text: Problem with the equipment from {chosenSupplier}. Nothing catastrophic — but it's not what we were promised.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You think, briefly, about the ones you didn't choose.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Funny thing about the budget you didn't spend on the extra filling line — turns out it's exactly what's needed now, with everything else that's landed on you since.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: I know I've pushed back on nearly everything you've proposed. For what it's worth — on this one, I think you're right. I'll back you with the Board if it comes to that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: News breaks that one of the suppliers you passed over — the fast, expensive one — has gone into administration after over-promising on a rival's contract.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Daniel doesn't say “I told you so.” He doesn't have to.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: Good instinct on the budget, actually.

lines.speaker: camille
lines.text: We do not have enough validation resource for two product lines on this timeline. That's not a risk. That's arithmetic.

lines.speaker: aisha
lines.text: One of the automation engineers just resigned. Effective immediately.

lines.speaker: aisha
lines.text: We've been locked out of the Building Management System. This isn't a glitch. It's an attack.

lines.speaker: daniel
lines.text: I'm freezing what's left of the contingency. I should have done it two months ago.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your validation engineer hands in her notice. A competitor made an offer she didn't want to refuse.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A post is circulating — claims the site is unsafe. It isn't true. It's spreading anyway.
